External impulse during the short collision is neglected, so the interaction only redistributes the carts' combined translational motion.

derivation_notes: The ideal point-mass latch law is refined by allowing off-axis capture geometry to divert part of the incoming relative motion into internal rotation during impact. A reduced-mass-weighted interaction between total translational motion and relative speed subtracts translational momentum available to the final shared motion, while vanishing when relative motion disappears.
change_summary: Changed the assumption that all pre-impact translational momentum remains in the final translational degree of freedom. The successor keeps the parent momentum-average structure but adds a joint dependence on total-motion scale and relative speed, representing rotational excitation during latching.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The carts behave as perfectly collinear point masses during latching, so no translational momentum is redistributed into offset rotational/internal motion.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Off-axis latch engagement or finite cart geometry causing part of the collision impulse to generate angular momentum/internal rotational motion, reducing the final center-of-mass translational share in a relative-speed-dependent way.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: When u1=u2, the interaction term is zero, so the successor exactly reduces to the parent expression.

response_change.parent_relation: The post-collision velocity is the mass-weighted average of the incoming velocities, depending only on total momentum and total mass.
response_change.child_relation: Retain momentum conservation but relax the point-mass assumption by allowing part of the incoming translational momentum to be carried in offset rotational degrees of freedom during latching, so the common translational velocity depends on masses and incoming velocities through an additional velocity-difference interaction.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed total incoming momentum, collisions with larger relative approach speed |u1-u2| produce systematically different common translational velocities than low-relative-speed collisions because more momentum is diverted into internal rotation; the parent predicts no such dependence.

evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, vary u1 and u2 while holding m1 and m2 fixed to compare equal-total-momentum collisions with different relative speeds; in holdout, extend to different mass ratios where the same relative-speed dependence is reweighted by reduced mass.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: In the zero-offset or zero-rotation-coupling limit, or when u1=u2 so there is no relative motion to excite internal rotation, the refinement collapses back to the parent law.

evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Off-axis latch engagement or finite cart geometry causing part of the collision impulse to generate angular momentum/internal rotational motion, reducing the final center-of-mass translational share in a relative-speed-dependent way.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the new term depends jointly on total-momentum scale and relative speed, so equal-momentum trials no longer collapse to one output. The mapping gains a genuine interaction across supplied inputs rather than a global rescaling.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: All pre-impact translational momentum remains in the final common translational degree of freedom under perfectly collinear point-mass capture.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Part of the incoming relative motion can be redirected into internal rotation during off-axis latching, altering the scored translational output itself.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: When u1=u2, the interaction term is zero, so the successor exactly reduces to the parent expression.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: For fixed m1 and m2, compare collisions with the same p_tot=m1*u1+m2*u2 but different u_rel=u1-u2. The parent gives identical v_post for all such trials, while the child predicts a systematic shift whose size grows with |u_rel| and is reweighted by mu_red=m1*m2/(m1+m2). This changes the target mapping itself, not just an auxiliary unobserved trajectory, and is observable only when capture geometry allows rotational excitation rather than perfectly central latching.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast because the parent target depends only on p_tot and m1+m2; it has no mechanism to distinguish two trials with identical total momentum but different relative speed. Refitting masses or any shared coefficient cannot create dependence on u1-u2 across those conditions without abandoning the parent structure.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The parent treats the carts as perfectly collinear point masses during latching, omitting the realistic possibility that an off-center or compliant latch converts some incoming relative motion into internal rotation while preserving total momentum.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the idealization that all pre-impact translational momentum remains in the final common translational degree of freedom; allow redistribution between translation and newly excited internal rotation during capture.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Off-axis latch engagement or finite cart geometry causing part of the collision impulse to generate angular momentum/internal rotational motion, reducing the final center-of-mass translational share in a relative-speed-dependent way.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent target mapping has a fixed-environment shortcut: for given m1 and m2 it maps (u1,u2) to v_post only through total momentum, so any two trials with the same m1*u1+m2*u2 must have the same output. A realistic next refinement is to account for capture geometry that lets relative approach motion excite internal rotation during latching. Vary u1 and u2 while holding m1 and m2 fixed and compare trials with the same total momentum but different relative speed |u1-u2|. The parent predicts identical v_post, whereas the child predicts a lower or otherwise shifted common translational velocity magnitude when |u1-u2| is larger because more of the incoming motion is diverted from translation into rotation. This is a genuine changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary trajectory change, because the scored output v_post itself changes as a function of already supplied inputs. The effect is scientifically admissible only when the latch geometry is not perfectly central and the carts can sustain some rotational/internal excitation; if the apparatus is well aligned so capture is strictly collinear, or if u1=u2 so relative motion vanishes, the refinement becomes unobservable and the parent law is recovered.

derivation_notes: The same reduced-mass relative-motion loss channel is retained, but the latch-engagement nonlinearity is refined from a single tanh of chi=(u1-u2)/v_cm to tanh(chi*(1+chi**2)), representing a weak onset at small slip and a steeper monotone activation at moderate slip before saturation. This keeps the mapping odd in relative speed and bounded while changing the curvature of the scored post-impact velocity with respect to the joint ratio of relative and center-of-mass motion.
change_summary: Changed the assumption that slip-driven translational loss has one universal tanh curvature. The successor uses a sharper monotone odd saturation in the same dimensionless slip ratio, producing stronger mid-range reduction in v_post while preserving the parent mechanism and saturation.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The relative-speed-induced loss channel follows one fixed tanh saturation shape over all admissible slip ratios.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Slip-dependent latch engagement can transfer translational motion into internal deformation or rotation more abruptly once relative speed becomes moderate compared with center-of-mass motion, while remaining monotone and dissipative.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The child approaches the parent effectively in the small-|chi| regime, where tanh(chi*(1+chi**2)) = chi + O(chi**3) and both laws share the same leading linear response.

response_change.parent_relation: The translational loss term is a single tanh saturation of relative speed normalized by the center-of-mass speed, so at fixed masses and center-of-mass motion the reduction in v_post depends on only one shared relative-speed scale.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the single tanh saturation with a sharper but still monotone odd dependence on the same relative-speed ratio, so the translational reduction turns on weakly at small mismatch and then steepens at moderate mismatch before saturating.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed m1,m2 and fixed (m1*u1+m2*u2)/(m1+m2), varying u1-u2 produces nearly parent-like v_post for small relative speed but a stronger mid-range drop in v_post at larger relative speed; one shared parent form cannot match both low- and mid-slip curvature simultaneously.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the center-of-mass speed is nonzero and |u1-u2| is comparable to or modestly larger than |(m1*u1+m2*u2)/(m1+m2)|, so the existing tanh argument is O(1); the change is weak in the small-slip limit and should not be claimed at v_cm≈0 where the parent normalization is singular.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Across training, modest |chi| shows both models close; in holdout with larger but admissible |chi| at similar masses and v_cm sign, the child predicts a steeper mid-range reduction before saturation, extending the same relative-slip mechanism rather than introducing a new branch.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: In the limit where the refined nonlinear shape parameter approaches its parent value, or in the small-|chi| regime where both odd saturating laws share the same leading linear term, the child reduces effectively to the parent response.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: nonlinear slip-dependent latch engagement during perfectly sticking collision
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Slip-dependent latch engagement can have a more abrupt transfer from mostly translational sticking to stronger rotational/internal deformation participation as relative speed grows, while remaining monotone, momentum-conserving, and energy-dissipative.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the nonlinear argument now depends jointly on the same declared relative-speed and center-of-mass quantities through chi and chi**3, changing curvature over input space rather than merely rescaling one existing term.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The relative-speed loss channel has one universal tanh curvature set only by chi=(u1-u2)/v_cm.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The same loss channel remains, but latch engagement sharpens with slip so the odd saturation depends on chi*(1+chi**2) rather than chi alone.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: For |(u1-u2)/((m1*u1+m2*u2)/(m1+m2))| << 1, the refined argument equals chi + O(chi**3), so the successor collapses to the parent's leading-order mapping.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Hold m1, m2, and v_cm=(m1*u1+m2*u2)/(m1+m2) fixed away from zero, and vary u_rel=u1-u2. Then the parent predicts one tanh-shaped reduction curve in chi, while the child stays close near chi=0 but bends downward more strongly for moderate |chi| before still saturating at large |chi|. This is a changed target mapping for v_post itself, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent tanh shape has one fixed curvature profile once masses and v_cm are fixed, so refitting all existing parent coefficients still cannot simultaneously preserve the gentle near-origin response and produce the steeper mid-range drop across admissible chi values. The mismatch is structural in the target mapping versus chi, not just numerical.

evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the assumption that the already-present relative-speed loss channel follows one universal tanh curvature over all admissible slip ratios.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Slip-dependent latch engagement can have a more abrupt transfer from mostly translational sticking to stronger rotational/internal deformation participation as relative speed grows, while remaining monotone, momentum-conserving, and energy-dissipative.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: for fixed m1,m2 and fixed center-of-mass speed v_cm, the scored target v_post decreases from the momentum-average value through a single odd saturating function of the ratio chi=(u1-u2)/v_cm. Proposed child change: keep the same physical channel—relative-motion-induced diversion of translational energy already used in the lineage—but replace the overly idealized one-shape saturation with a sharper monotone odd curvature. Distinguishing condition: vary relative speed u1-u2 while holding m1, m2, and v_cm approximately fixed and away from zero. Then compare small-to-moderate |chi| against larger moderate |chi|. Limitation: the contrast should only be claimed where v_cm is not too small, since the current normalization makes chi ill-conditioned near zero center-of-mass motion.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when the center-of-mass speed remains finite and nonzero and the relative speed spans from small to order-comparable with that drift, so the transition region in r is sampled rather than only the near-linear or fully saturated limits.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate |r| already reveals whether the correction bends with one smooth tanh profile or with a delayed steeper transition; in holdout, larger |r| extends the same monotone mechanism into the stronger-loss regime without changing the underlying process.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: In the limit where the sharpened switching law reduces to the original tanh profile, or equivalently when its extra shape deformation tends to zero, the parent relation is recovered.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model already includes slip-dependent diversion of relative motion into rotational/internal modes, but it assumes one fixed tanh transition shape; real latch engagement and deformation can activate more abruptly over an intermediate slip band than that single smoothness allows.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The fraction of relative motion diverted from common translation is represented by one specific tanh-shaped monotone saturation with a single built-in curvature profile.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Nonlinear latch seating and compliance can produce a sharper onset of rotational/internal participation after initial stick-like engagement, while remaining smooth, momentum-conserving, bounded, and dissipative.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed transition-shape assumption rather than add a new process. The parent maps inputs to v_post through the momentum-average term minus a monotone correction governed by a single tanh-like threshold in the dimensionless ratio r=(u1-u2)/v_cm. Vary relative speed u1-u2 while holding m1, m2, and v_cm fixed. Then the parent enforces one specific curvature: the loss term begins smoothly and approaches saturation with one shared steepness pattern. The child would keep the same physical mechanism—relative-speed-driven transfer into rotational/internal motion—but allow a sharper smooth crossover. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory: v_post versus r acquires different curvature and intermediate-slope behavior. The contrast is scientifically admissible when v_cm is not near zero and |r| crosses the activation band from small slip to O(1) slip. A single refit of the parent's existing shape cannot generally reproduce both weak-loss behavior at small |r| and a steeper intermediate drop at larger |r| if those curvatures differ systematically, because the parent has only one built-in transition profile. The parent remains recoverable as the sharper law is relaxed back to the original tanh form.

scenario_text: Two carts moving along one straight track collide and latch together. The target is the common velocity immediately after impact, inferred from the independently chosen masses and incoming signed velocities. External impulse during the short collision is neglected, so the interaction only redistributes the carts' combined translational motion.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed masses and center-of-mass speed, the correction to the momentum-average post-collision velocity is a single tanh-shaped monotone function of relative speed ratio, so one shared saturation scale controls the whole transition from weak to strong translational loss.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same relative-speed-controlled rotational/internal-loss mechanism, but replace the single tanh transition by a sharper asymmetric smooth switching law so the correction grows gently at small slip and then steepens over an intermediate slip band before saturating, changing the curvature of v_post versus relative-speed ratio.
response_change.observable_effect: When masses and center-of-mass speed are held fixed while relative speed is swept, the child predicts a delayed-but-steeper drop of post-collision translational velocity over a finite slip range, whereas the parent can only give one fixed smoothness profile with one shared transition shape.

evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than coefficient retuning because the nonlinear slip map is now nested with a mass-symmetry factor inside both the rational curvature term and the tanh argument, so the response surface cannot be reduced to one universal function of slip alone.

evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Recover the parent law in the limit that the mass-asymmetry dependence vanishes, so the slip-response shape becomes independent of mass ratio and only the original normalized relative-speed transition remains.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed vcm and comparable slip_ratio, plotting v_post against slip_ratio for several mass_symmetry classes gives a family of monotone curves with different mid-range curvature: mass_symmetry near 1 bends away from the momentum-average sooner and more strongly than low-mass_symmetry cases. evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set is structurally inadequate because the parent compresses the response into one universal function of slip_ratio only. evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The refinement is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it introduces a competing higher-order loss contribution that is selectively strong only in the joint region of large normalized severity and high mass symmetry, changing curvature of the scored input-output surface rather than merely rescaling it globally.
